title: Add streaming data loader for datasets that exceed RAM
description:
Currently the data loader in prepare.py loads all training shards into memory before training begins. This works on machines with abundant RAM but fails on systems with less than ~16 GB free, as the full dataset can exceed available memory.

Implement a streaming data loader that:
  - Reads shards from disk on demand rather than preloading
  - Maintains the same interface as the existing make_dataloader function (drop-in replacement)
  - Supports the best-fit packing strategy already implemented (pack sequences to fill the context window)
  - Prefetches the next shard in a background thread to hide I/O latency
  - Handles the case where a shard file is missing or corrupt (log a warning and skip)

The existing non-streaming loader should remain as a fallback, selectable via a parameter. The default behavior should NOT change for users who have enough RAM (i.e., detect available memory and choose automatically, or expose a `streaming=True` argument).

Do NOT change the evaluation function evaluate_bpb() or the validation data loading path — only training data loading is in scope.
acceptance_criteria: make_dataloader accepts a streaming=True keyword argument
Streaming mode loads shards lazily (only one shard in RAM at a time)
Background prefetch thread is used to hide I/O latency
Best-fit packing is preserved in streaming mode
Missing or corrupt shards are skipped with a logged warning
evaluate_bpb() and the validation loader are untouched
